reasoning_trace.value: The proposed system integrates a Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) with an ISAC-enabled base station to enable secure and efficient data transmission in dynamic aquatic environments. The RIS is composed of passive elements that can be programmed to introduce phase shifts, allowing for beamforming and null steering. The system uses a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to predict environmental parameters such as salinity and turbulence, which are then used to inform the Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) agent. The DRL agent selects candidate RIS phase-shift configurations that maximize secrecy rate and energy efficiency while minimizing bit error rate (BER). The NSGA-II optimizer refines these configurations to achieve Pareto-optimal solutions that balance secrecy rate and energy efficiency.

reasoning_trace.value: The proposed system addresses the challenges of underwater optical wireless communication (UOWC) by integrating a Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) with an ISAC-enabled base station. The system uses a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to predict environmental parameters, a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) agent to select RIS phase-shift configurations, and an NSGA-II optimizer to refine these configurations. The system achieves significant improvements in secrecy rate, bit error rate, and reconfiguration latency. However, open challenges remain, such as scaling the system to larger RIS arrays, maintaining real-time operation, and addressing the impact of biofouling on RIS surface reflectivity.
